title: Efficient Multilingual Language Model Compression through Vocabulary Trimming
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured social bias in religious contexts by evaluating the pseudo-likelihood scores of language models for stereotypical versus anti-stereotypical sentences related to religion.
findings: The monolingual model (RoBERTa) exhibited higher levels of social bias compared to the multilingual model (XLM-R). For the 'religion' bias category specifically, RoBERTa showed a stereotypical bias score of 54.4 on the StereoSet (SS) dataset, while XLM-R showed an anti-stereotypical bias score of 46.8. On the CrowS-Pairs (CP) dataset, XLM-R's score (54.3) was slightly more stereotypical than RoBERTa's (53.3). The proposed vocabulary trimming method did not significantly alter the social bias scores of the original multilingual model.
